rule.inputs: saved post rows, error items read back from each run dataset (get-dataset-items on error fields; free read), actor run record (get-actor-run), profile check record
rule.a: at least one in-window row, fewer than 200 rows for the account, run SUCCEEDED, run did not hit its cap
rule.b: no in-window row AND (the actor returned at least one older row, i.e. a pinned post, OR the profile check reports 0 total posts)
rule.c: profile or post scraper returned "Restricted profile" or a private/restricted account error attributed to that account (inputUrl); never counted as a zero-post clinic
rule.d: no rows and no error item for the account, or its run failed/aborted/timed out, or the run hit maxTotalChargeUsd before the account produced a result; retry only these inside budget
rule.e: no_items for an account whose profile was public with posts (ambiguous: no in-window posts or hidden data), a run that hit its cap with partial rows, 200 or more rows, or anything the evidence cannot settle; sub-label probable_no_in_window_posts when the profile was public with posts
rule.attribution: no_items items carry inputUrl; restricted_page items carry no inputUrl, so they cannot be attributed to an account and are only a run-level flag
rule.limits: The scraper filters by onlyPostsNewerThan, so the oldest returned in-window post is never older than the window start; whether the window was fully covered cannot be observed from rows. No run hit its cap (largest pilot run 209 items, about 0.48 USD estimated against a 1.00 cap). Row count under 200 is necessary but not sufficient, and is recorded as such. Billed charges are unavailable, so cap hits are inferred from estimated row cost and status SUCCEEDED, not read from billing.
